deep.reconstruction:
Problem: count the cyclic arrangements (necklaces) of a+b places carrying a objects of one kind and b of the other, counted up to rotation. Equivalently, count the orbits of the cyclic group Z/(a+b) acting on the C(a+b,a) binary words. The next page confirms this reading: it carries the general Möbius-type bookkeeping 'für v, qv, q^2 v, pqv, ...' and the final sum (1/v)[...].

(1) Coprime case, gcd(a,b)=1 ('a rel. prim zu b'). No word is fixed by a nontrivial rotation, so every orbit has exactly a+b elements. The number of necklaces is C(a+b,a)/(a+b) = (a+b)!/(a! b! (a+b)).

(2) Case a = p*alpha, b = p*beta, with p prime and gcd(alpha,beta)=1 (both assumptions are implicit). A word whose period divides alpha+beta is determined by its first alpha+beta letters, so there are C(alpha+beta,alpha) such words. Their orbits have size alpha+beta.
- The remaining C(a+b,a) - C(alpha+beta,alpha) words have minimal period a+b, with orbits of size a+b.
- Number of necklaces N = [C(a+b,a) - C(alpha+beta,alpha)]/(a+b) + C(alpha+beta,alpha)/(alpha+beta).
- Riemann rewrites this, correctly, as N = (a+b-1)!/(a! b!) + (alpha+beta-1)!/(alpha! beta!) * (1 - 1/p).
- [My check] This is exactly the Cauchy–Frobenius/Burnside count N = (1/(p(alpha+beta))) [C(p(alpha+beta), p alpha) + (p-1) C(alpha+beta,alpha)], i.e. the case n = p(alpha+beta) of (1/n) sum_{d | gcd(a,b)} phi(d) C(n/d, a/d).

(3) Integral representation of the binomial coefficients (Cauchy coefficient extraction). Riemann notes (1/2pi) ∫_{-pi}^{pi} x^{-n} f(x) dphi with x = r e^{i phi}, and (1+x)^{a+b} = sum x^a (a+b)!/(a! b!). Hence C(a+b,a) = (1/2pi) ∫ x^{-a} (1+x)^{a+b} dphi.
- He puts z = (r e^{i phi})^{-alpha} (1 + r e^{i phi})^{alpha+beta}.
- Then z^m = x^{-m alpha} (1+x)^{m(alpha+beta)}, so (1/2pi) ∫ z^m dphi = C(m(alpha+beta), m alpha).

(4) Case a = pq*alpha, b = pq*beta, with p, q distinct primes [assumption mine/implicit]. Counting words by exact (minimal) period:
- period alpha+beta: C(alpha+beta,alpha) = (1/2pi) ∫ z dphi;
- period q(alpha+beta): C(q alpha+q beta, q alpha) - C(alpha+beta,alpha) = (1/2pi) ∫ (z^q - z) dphi;
- period p(alpha+beta): C(p alpha+p beta, p alpha) - C(alpha+beta,alpha) = (1/2pi) ∫ (z^p - z) dphi;
- period pq(alpha+beta): (1/2pi) ∫ (z^pq - z^q - z^p + z) dphi. This is inclusion–exclusion, i.e. Möbius inversion over the divisors of pq; the total of all four classes is C(a+b,a).

(5) The necklace number is then obtained, as on the next page, by dividing each class by its period length and summing:
N = (1/v)[(z^pq - z^p - z^q + z)/(pq) + (z^p - z)/p + (z^q - z)/q + z], with v = alpha+beta and [ ] denoting the constant term (1/2pi) ∫ ... dphi.

The page is thus a derivation of the fixed-content binary necklace formula via Möbius inversion on periods, with binomial coefficients written as contour integrals.
errors: No substantive errors. The formulas tacitly assume gcd(alpha,beta)=1, and that p and q are distinct primes; for prime powers the next page treats q, q^2, q^3 separately.
The labels 'Die Periode q(alpha+beta) haben' mean words of exact (minimal) period q(alpha+beta), not words whose period divides q(alpha+beta). With that reading the differences are correct.
In '(1+x)^{a+b} = sum x^a (a+b)!/(a!b!)' the letter a is used as the summation index (with b = n - a). This is loose but harmless.
The final integral (z^pq - z^q - z^p + z) counts words, not necklaces; division by pq(alpha+beta) and summation with the other classes is carried out only on the next page.

results.what: Number of necklaces with a beads of one colour and b of another, gcd(a,b)=1: C(a+b,a)/(a+b)
results.modern_name: binary necklaces with fixed content (coprime case)
results.usually_credited_to: folklore; classical (MacMahon 1892, also implicit in Fermat-type necklace proofs)

results.modern_name: Cauchy–Frobenius–Burnside orbit count; special case of N = (1/n) sum_{d|gcd(a,b)} phi(d) C(n/d,a/d)
results.usually_credited_to: MacMahon (1892) / Jablonski (1892) for the general fixed-content necklace formula; orbit-counting lemma Cauchy 1845, Frobenius 1887

results.what: Binomial coefficients as constant terms (1/2pi) ∫ z^m dphi with z = x^{-alpha}(1+x)^{alpha+beta}
Words of exact period pq(alpha+beta) counted by inclusion–exclusion: C(pq v, pq alpha) - C(q v, q alpha) - C(p v, p alpha) + C(v, alpha)
results.modern_name: Möbius inversion over periods (primitive words / Lyndon words with fixed content)
results.usually_credited_to: Moreau 1872 (necklace polynomial), Möbius function in number theory 1832; fixed-content version MacMahon / Witt

deep.surprise_reason: Riemann is here (c.1853) working out the fixed-content binary necklace count via Möbius inversion on periods, with a Burnside-type closed form for n = p(alpha+beta). The mathematics is elementary, but it predates Moreau (1872) and MacMahon (1892), and combinatorial enumeration of this kind is not part of Riemann's recognized work. It is a notable unpublished detail rather than a major discovery; Gauss had similar Möbius-type counts earlier.

transcription_corrections: '175' at the top right is the folio number, not part of a formula.
In the first line the struck-out symbol after (a+b) is a deleted character before the '!'; the intended expression is (a+b)!/(a!b!) * 1/(a+b).
The definition reads z = (r e^{phi i})^{-alpha} (1 + r e^{phi i})^{alpha+beta}; a struck '1/alpha' or similar above the first factor is deleted.
In the line for period q(alpha+beta), the integrand is (z^q - z); the second term is partly overwritten in the image.
The line '[-...-]^n pq' near the bottom is a struck symbol with exponent n, followed by 'pq'; it is apparently an abandoned start of the general case.
